observation.visible_scene: A tight close-up of a drum kit in a warmly lit room. A large, slightly out-of-focus cymbal on its stand dominates the left foreground; a snare drum sits at the bottom left, a wood-finish tom with a round badge at center-right, and a hi-hat plus another angled cymbal on the right. Behind the kit a seated drummer in a grey long-sleeve top and dark trousers holds two drumsticks, their hands partly hidden by the foreground cymbal. A piano and a folded blue cloth are visible in the static background.
visible_changes: Throughout the excerpt the drummer's hands and sticks move in a fast, rhythmic up-and-down pattern; at several moments (e.g. t≈0.12, 0.24, 0.52, 0.64, 0.92, 1.40, 1.60) the motion is so quick the hands and stick tips blur.

The sticks alternate between a near-vertical orientation (tip pointing down toward the tom, e.g. t≈0.08, 0.20, 1.28–1.44) and a more horizontal orientation held across the body (e.g. t≈0.56–0.60, 0.96–1.24), consistent with alternating strokes.
The hands periodically drop out of view behind the foreground cymbal (e.g. t≈0.36–0.48, 0.72–0.84) and reappear, indicating occlusion rather than disappearance.
The drummer's torso and arms shift slightly with the playing motion (leaning and arm extension), while the drum shells, hardware, stands and background piano remain in fixed positions.
The large foreground cymbal shows small, frame-to-frame changes in tilt/edge position, suggesting it is vibrating/wobbling, though no direct stick contact with it is clearly captured.
The camera framing stays essentially constant across all frames; the background elements do not translate, so the visible motion is object/hand motion, not camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: The actual sound, tempo and musical pattern are not observable.
Which specific drum or cymbal each stroke lands on is largely hidden by the foreground cymbal and motion blur.
The moments just before t=0 and after t=1.60 are outside the segment; the playing is already ongoing at the start and continues at the end.
uncertain_details: Whether the foreground cymbal's positional jitter is genuine post-strike vibration or a slight camera/handheld shake cannot be resolved from these frames alone.
Exact contact points of the stick tips are obscured by occlusion and blur, so precise strike locations are inferred only loosely.
The left hand is more often hidden than the right, so its full motion path is partially uncertain.

the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.

do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.

camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
